issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a String (and Part 2 explicitly describes the method returning the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), and the template Main prints the return value of messageOnMilk(); however, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a boolean and Seal/Goat implement it by printing to stdout and returning true. This return-type mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students and prevents them from implementing the intended behavior (returning the milk message as a String).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API with the problem specification: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String, and update implementations (Seal, Goat) to return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" rather than printing and returning boolean. Ensure any call sites (e.g., Main and tests) print the returned String. Alternatively, if the boolean-return design is intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify a boolean return and clarify that the message should be printed inside the method.

issues.description: The exercise specification (UML and textual requirements) defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning a String (the lyric: "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). In the provided solution, Milkable.messageOnMilk() is declared to return a boolean and the implementations (Seal, Goat) print the milking message and return true. This mismatch in the method's return type and expected behavior prevents a clear mapping from the problem requirements to the solution API and will confuse students about the expected contract of the Milkable interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Milkable interface in the solution to declare messageOnMilk() returning String (String messageOnMilk()). Update Seal and Goat to return the expected string (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked" / "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. This will align the solution's API and implementations with the problem specification and make the intended contract explicit for students.
